facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s with a 10-year history of Crohn disease
had intermittent bowel obstructions leading to total proctocolectomy and ileostomy
Five weeks after his surgery, he developed a painful, erosive lesion around his stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
No additional cutaneous or mucosal lesions were present
Repeated cultures were negative
Revealed epidermal erosion with suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis
Direct immunofluorescence of perilesional skin showed intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis
Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay showed high level of IgG autoantibodies
Against desmoglein 1: 40 IU/mL (normal value: 20 U/mL)
Against desmoglein 3: 90 IU/mL (normal value: 20 U/mL)
A painful, erosive lesion around the stoma on the anterior abdominal wall
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showing suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis (original magnification ×100)

concepts.why: High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 1 and 3, and intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis, are characteristic of Pemphigus vulgaris.
The development of a painful, erosive lesion around the stoma site is a known complication of stoma formation.
The patient's history of Crohn disease and subsequent development of bowel obstructions leading to total proctocolectomy and ileostomy increase the risk of complications.
The presence of autoantibodies and intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis suggests an autoimmune bullous disease.
The development of a painful, erosive lesion around the stoma site could be indicative of a surgical site infection, although repeated cultures were negative.
The presence of a painful, erosive lesion around the stoma site, along with a history of Crohn disease, could suggest pyoderma gangrenosum.
The development of a painful, erosive lesion around the stoma site, in a patient with a history of Crohn disease, is consistent with peristomal pyoderma gangrenosum.
The presence of autoantibodies and a history of Crohn disease could suggest an autoimmune enteropathy.
It explains the histopathological finding of suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis and the presence of autoantibodies against desmoglein 1.

rationales.F01: 10-year history of Crohn disease may be related to Crohn disease-related complications
rationales.F03: Painful, erosive lesion around stoma is a common symptom of pemphigus vulgaris and peristomal pyoderma gangrenosum
rationales.F05: Negative microbiological cultures rule out surgical site infection
rationales.F06: Suprabasal epidermal splitting with acantholysis is a characteristic histopathological feature of pemphigus vulgaris
rationales.F07: Intercellular deposition of IgG and C3 throughout epidermis is a characteristic immunofluorescence pattern of pemphigus vulgaris
rationales.F10: High levels of IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 are characteristic of pemphigus vulgaris
